summary: This 3-page paper presents a formal-verification and exact-rational auditing companion stack for Sälzer's recent NEXPTIME-hardness proof for degree-<=3 local-sum ReLU MPNN satisfiability [5]. It combines (i) 18 zero-sorry, zero-Classical.choice Lean 4.35.0 theorems covering cleared-denominator tape encoding/pop disambiguation, polyhedron counts, ReLU-min polyhedral union exactness, and binary-tree degree/dimension/acceptance identities, with (ii) an exact-Q Python verifier (MPNN-DEGBSAT-CERT-1.0) tested on 16 canonical certificates (up to h=3, 8 NTM steps) and 62 adversarial forgery attacks (62/62 rejected). All stated algebraic identities and plotted exact-rational profiles (Fig. 1a, Fig. 2a, Mode 1 fractions, and 62/62 attack counts) check out mathematically, with only minor presentation/numerical discrepancies (notably Mode 4's 16.67 ms h=2 latency in Fig. 2b/3a omitted from the 18.112-114.497 ms text range) and an overstated title relative to the explicitly scoped non-complexity Lean formalization.
weaknesses: The title ('Certified Verification of NEXPTIME-Hardness...') overstates the scope of the Lean 4 formalization, which explicitly excludes complexity-class reductions, NTM semantics, and time hierarchies.
Lean 4.35.0 proofs are proved over cleared-denominator N, Z, and List Int rather than directly over Q, leaving the rational bridge and full NTM/MPNN execution to the unmechanized Python verifier.

The 3-page summary omits the exact Lean theorem signatures, concrete polyhedron matrices, and NTM transition tables (e.g., the Mode 4 soundness witness yielding error 3/5 from a +1/5 perturbation), limiting full standalone auditability from the PDF alone.
Section 3's rational parsing rule ('reduced denominators >= 2') is slightly ambiguous regarding how integer constants (such as 0 and 1 in polyhedra and MPNN outputs) are encoded in JSON payloads.
